q: The Namsan cable car has been running since…
fact: It opened in 1962 — Korea's first passenger cable car. The cabins have been replaced several times; the route hasn't.

q: The colour of N Seoul Tower's lights at night tells you…
a: How many visitors are up there
fact: Blue means the fine-dust level is good. Red or purple? Maybe skip the deep breaths on the terrace.

q: What do couples traditionally do with the key after locking a love lock on Namsan?
fact: Thousands of keys were tossed down the hill until the city installed key bins. Bring a lock; leave the key in the bin, not the forest.

q: Why is the Namsan donkatsu so famous with Seoul taxi drivers?
a: It's huge, cheap and fast — a driver's lunch
It comes with free petrol vouchers
The owner used to drive a taxi
It's the only place open at 4 am
fact: The plate-sized, thin wang-donkkaseu started as a cabbies' lunch spot below the cable car in the 1990s, then went viral with everyone else.

q: How many dishes are on the menu at Myeongdong Kyoja?
fact: Just four: kalguksu, mandu, bibim-guksu and kongguksu. They've held a Michelin Bib Gourmand for years with that menu.

q: 'Nogari' — the snack that gives Euljiro's alley its name — is…
fact: Dried baby pollack, grilled and torn by hand, dipped in gochujang-mayo, with draught beer. The alley is a registered 'Seoul Future Heritage'.

q: Gyeongbokgung's name means roughly…
fact: 景福 — 'shining happiness / great blessing'. It was the first Joseon palace, founded in 1395, and burned and rebuilt more than once.

q: The royal guard-changing ceremony at the gate is…
fact: It's a faithful 1996 re-enactment based on Joseon records — the uniforms, drums and flags are historically researched, the guards are performers.

q: Cheonggyecheon stream was, until 2005…
a: A sewer open to the sky
fact: A highway ran right on top of it. The restoration pulled out the road and uncovered 10 km of stream — the water is pumped in from the Han.

q: The National Folk Museum is famous for an outdoor street recreating…
fact: The 'Street of Memories' has a 1970s comic-book shop, a barber and a tea room — the 'Memories' of your parents' Seoul.

q: Samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) is traditionally eaten on…
fact: 'Fight heat with heat' — Koreans queue for the hot soup on the three bok days of summer. Tosokchon's queue is long all year anyway.

q: Bukchon means…
fact: 北村 — the village north of the stream, between the two palaces, where high officials lived. Around 900 hanok still stand there.

q: Jogyesa's courtyard is famous in spring and autumn for…
fact: The white pine (baeksong) is Natural Monument No. 9 and roughly five centuries old. In May the yard fills with thousands of paper lanterns.

q: Gaeseong-style dumplings (the ones at Koong) are known for being…
a: Big and round, filled with tofu and pork
fact: Gaeseong is now in North Korea — the recipe came south with the family. One dumpling is nearly a meal; they're the size of a fist.

q: The glasshouse at Changgyeonggung was built in 1909 as…
a: A tea pavilion for the Japanese governor
fact: The Grand Greenhouse was Korea's first Western glasshouse — now a cast-iron-and-glass jewel full of winter orchids and chrysanthemums.

q: Buried in Namsangol Hanok Village is a time capsule to be opened in…
fact: Sealed in 1994 for Seoul's 600th birthday with 600 everyday objects — to be opened on the 1000th, in 2394.

q: According to a Seoul legend, couples who walk the Deoksugung stone-wall road will…
fact: The old family court sat at the end of the road, so couples 'walking it together' were headed for divorce. The court has moved. Hold hands.

q: Deoksugung is unusual among Seoul's palaces because it has…
fact: Emperor Gojong built Seokjojeon, a neoclassical stone hall, in 1910 — a Joseon palace with Corinthian columns.

q: How wide is the Han River where it crosses Seoul?
fact: Roughly a kilometre — wider than the Seine, Thames and Spree combined. That's why the city built 30-odd bridges and one island (Yeouido).

q: The Banpo Bridge fountain holds a Guinness record as…
fact: 1,140 m of nozzles along both sides of the bridge — 380 of them — spraying 190 tonnes of river water a minute, lit in rainbow colours.

q: What does the Han River convenience store have that most don't?
fact: Pay ₩1,000, press start, and the machine boils your instant noodles. Add egg and a cheese slice — it's the river ritual.

q: Jokbal — Seongsu's speciality — is…
fact: Trotters simmered for hours in soy, ginger and spices, sliced thin and wrapped in lettuce with shrimp sauce. Collagen for days.

q: Seongsu-dong is nicknamed the … of Seoul
fact: Old shoe factories and warehouses turned into cafés, galleries and pop-up stores — Cafe Onion itself was a metal-parts factory.

q: Seoul Forest's most photographed residents are…
fact: A herd of deer lives in a large enclosure you can feed — plus the ginkgo tree avenue that goes gold at the end of October.

q: How many drones fly in the Hangang show finale?
fact: Two thousand drones form shapes over the river — this year's finale is Marvel-themed. The main 10-minute show is around 20:30.

q: In a jjimjilbang you'll see people wearing towels folded into…
fact: The 'yangmeori' (sheep head) towel — rolled at both ends — is a K-drama staple. Eat baked eggs and sikhye while wearing one.

q: Lotte World Tower (Seoul Sky) is how tall?
fact: 555 m and 123 floors — the tallest building in Korea and the sixth tallest in the world. The glass floor on 118 is 478 m up.

q: The giant Rubber Duck that floated on Seokchon Lake in 2014 was…
a: A real inflatable duck for kids
fact: Florentijn Hofman's 16.5-metre duck drew 5 million visitors in a month. The lake is also the cherry-blossom hotspot in April.

q: The 'lone tree' in Olympic Park stands on…
fact: Mongchontoseong is a Baekje-era earth wall from around the 3rd century — the lone juniper on top is Seoul's favourite wedding-photo spot.

q: Top speed of the KTX between Seoul and Busan?
fact: 305 km/h in service — the 400 km trip takes about 2 h 40 with stops. The trains are French TGV cousins; the newer KTX-Sancheon are Korean-built.

q: Busan's milmyeon noodles were born out of…
a: Korean War refugees who had no buckwheat
fact: Refugees from the north wanted naengmyeon but had only US-aid wheat flour — so the cold-noodle recipe went wheat. It's Busan's summer dish.

q: Dwaeji gukbap — Busan's soul food — is…
fact: Milky pork-bone broth with rice, best with saeujeot (salted shrimp) and a pile of chives. Also a refugee-era invention, now a Busan religion.

q: Gwangan Bridge's nickname is…
fact: 7.4 km long, lit in changing colours every night — locals just call it Diamond Bridge. It even hosts the November fireworks festival.

q: At Millak Raw Fish Market, you buy fish downstairs and then…
a: Carry it upstairs and pay a table charge to eat it
Grill it yourself on the beach
Give it to the chef to cook for free
fact: Pick the fish on the ground floor, agree a price, and a restaurant upstairs slices it for a small per-person table charge (₩5k).

q: The Blueline Park track used to be…
fact: An old railway along the cliffs, abandoned in 2013, reopened in 2020 as the beach train and the sky capsules you ride today.

q: 'Daritdol' in Cheongsapo Daritdol Skywalk means…
fact: The five rocks off the shore look like stepping stones (daritdol) — the 72 m glass-floored walkway lets you 'step' over them.

q: Bokguk is a soup made from…
fact: Pufferfish (bok) — the potentially lethal one. Licensed chefs remove the toxin; the clear soup with bean sprouts is Busan's hangover cure.

q: What makes Haedong Yonggungsa unusual among Korean temples?
a: It's built on the sea cliffs, not in the mountains
fact: Almost every Korean temple is in the mountains; this one from 1376 sits on the rocks with waves below. Toss a coin into the stone bowl for luck.

q: BUSAN X the SKY sits on floors…
fact: Floors 98 to 100 of the LCT Landmark Tower, 411 m up — with the world's highest Starbucks on 99.

q: The 'Dongbaek' in Dongbaekseom is…
fact: Camellias — they bloom red on the island in winter. The 2005 APEC summit house is on the point, and there's a mermaid statue.

q: Gamcheon Culture Village began as…
a: A hillside refugee settlement in the 1950s
fact: Korean War refugees built the stacked houses up the hillside. In 2009 artists painted it — now it's the 'Machu Picchu of Busan'.

q: The Little Prince statue in Gamcheon is looking at…
fact: He sits on the wall with the fox beside him, gazing over the village. Expect a 20-minute photo queue — it's the icon.

q: Jagalchi, Korea's largest fish market, is famous for its…
a: Market 'ajumma' — the women who run it
fact: The 'Jagalchi ajumma' have run the stalls since the war years. Buy downstairs, eat it grilled upstairs on the 2nd floor.

q: Busan's hotteok (sold at BIFF Square) differs from Seoul's because it's filled with…
fact: Ssiat hotteok: the fried pancake is cut open and stuffed with sunflower, pumpkin seeds and peanuts. ₩2,000 of happiness.

q: Huinnyeoul means…
fact: Streams once ran down the cliff like white rapids. Now it's the 'Santorini of Busan' — a cliff-edge lane of white houses, seen in the film 'The Attorney'.

q: The Songdo Marine Cable Car crosses…
fact: 1.6 km over the water from the beach to Amnam Park, up to 86 m above the sea. Pick a 'Crystal Cruise' cabin for the glass floor.

q: Taejongdae is named after…
a: King Taejong, who practised archery there
fact: King Taejong of Silla reportedly came to shoot arrows on the cliffs. On clear days you can see Tsushima, Japan, from the lighthouse.

q: Spa Land is inside…
fact: Shinsegae Centum City held the Guinness record for the largest department store. Spa Land has 22 baths from two different hot springs.

q: Samjin Eomuk is…
fact: Founded 1953 in Busan — fish cake (eomuk) is a Busan speciality. Their bakery-style shop at the station sells croquette fish cakes to take on the train.

q: The Seoul City Wall (Hanyangdoseong) was originally…
a: 18.6 km around the four inner mountains
fact: 18.6 km of wall over Bugaksan, Naksan, Namsan and Inwangsan, started in 1396. The Naksan stretch is the easiest and prettiest at sunset.

q: Bindaetteok at Gwangjang Market is made from…
fact: Mung beans are ground on stone mills right at the stall, then fried in a lot of oil. Dip in soy-onion sauce; add makgeolli.

q: Yukhoe is…
a: Raw seasoned beef, often with raw egg
fact: Hand-cut raw beef with sesame oil, pear and a raw yolk. Gwangjang's 'yukhoe alley' has had a Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2017.

q: Dongdaemun Design Plaza was designed by…
fact: Zaha Hadid's silver 'spaceship' opened in 2014 on the site of the old baseball stadium — 45,000 aluminium panels, no two alike.

q: Changdeokgung is a UNESCO site because…
a: It was built to follow the natural landscape
fact: Unlike the formal grid of Gyeongbokgung, it bends around the hills and streams — hence the Secret Garden (Huwon) behind it.

q: The Secret Garden pond pavilion, Buyongjeong, is shaped like…
fact: Buyong means lotus; the pavilion's two legs stand in the square pond with its round island — earth and heaven in Joseon cosmology.

q: Ikseon-dong's hanok were built in the…
fact: Developer Jeong Se-gwon built small hanok for ordinary Koreans in the 1920s so the area wouldn't fall to Japanese developers. Now it's café lanes.

q: Jongmyo Shrine holds…
a: The spirit tablets of Joseon kings and queens
fact: The 109 m main hall — the longest wooden building in Korea — holds spirit tablets of 19 kings and 30 queens. The ritual music is UNESCO-listed too.

q: The proper way to eat Korean BBQ pork is…
a: Wrapped in lettuce with garlic and ssamjang, in one bite
fact: Ssam: lettuce or perilla leaf, pork, a slice of garlic, ssamjang, maybe kimchi — fold and eat in one bite. Never two bites.

q: Incheon Airport has been voted the world's best airport…
fact: It won the ACI best-airport award 12 years in a row. Allow time: there's a Korean culture museum, a spa and an ice rink inside.

q: Myeongdong's name means…
fact: 明洞 — 'bright cave/town'. It's Korea's most expensive real estate and the street-food stalls open around 16:00.

q: Gwangalli Beach is famous for…
a: Its view of the lit Gwangan Bridge
fact: The 1.4 km beach faces straight at Diamond Bridge — the Saturday drone show happens here (you'll miss it, but the lights are nightly).

q: Daehangno — the area of your glue hotel — is Seoul's…
fact: 'University Street' (Seoul National University was here) became the home of small theatres — more than 150 around Marronnier Park.
